subject: Prefix cache invalidation — temporary latency spike (status update)
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Brenner <alex@stellardata.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: [Redwood] Incident notification — increased latency due to prefix cache invalidation

Hi Alex / Taylor,

Wanted to let you know we observed a spike in request latencies (and an elevated 5xx rate) affecting the Hosted Inference API starting at ~07:50 PT this morning. We pushed an initial mitigation around 08:05 that reduced error rates but we are still seeing longer tails for some generation requests.

We have published a brief status update: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-12-04-prefix-cache.

What happened (brief): an automated prefix/KV cache invalidation routine ran while a higher-than-usual burst of long-sequence generation traffic was active. That caused a temporary increase in per-request CPU and memory pressure on a subset of serving nodes, which lengthened response times and caused retries that cascaded.

Immediate customer impact: some requests experienced latency above your 95th/99th SLOs and a small fraction (~0.8%) returned 502/503 for short windows. We do not have evidence of data loss or model corruption.

Next steps:
- Engineering is doing a root-cause triage and we will post a more complete timeline and mitigation details by EOD.
- I will keep you updated on the status page; we expect a full remediation by EOD Pacific but will confirm as we validate.

Attachments: incident_timeline_v1.pdf (initial timeline), mitigation-checklist.txt

Sorry for the disruption — I know this impacts your ingestion pipeline. If you want, we can open a dedicated support bridge; Sam from our SRE team can join.

Regards,
Mateo
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: incident_timeline_v1.pdf (PDF)]

From: Alex Brenner <alex@stellardata.com>

Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 08:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: [Redwood] Incident notification — increased latency due to prefix cache invalidation

Thanks Mateo — we just started seeing increased error rates on our end around 07:58 PT. Production inference jobs for our recommendations service were backfilled but customers noticed a 30–40s tail on some suggestions.

Can you confirm:
- Are you throttling or failing requests or just returning 5xx from the inference tier?
- Is there any mitigation we should do client-side (backoff settings, smaller batch sizes) while you stabilize?

If helpful, we can hold on a quick bridge — Taylor (cc'd) is Ops and can join.

— Alex
Senior SRE, Stellar Data

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, ops@stellardata.com
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 08:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: [Redwood] Incident notification — increased latency due to prefix cache invalidation

Hi Alex — quick answers:
- Most customer errors were transient 502/503 responses from a subset of inference nodes; we did not intentionally throttle client requests beyond normal rate limits.
- Short term client-side actions: enable exponential backoff for retries (recommended base 200ms, cap 5s) and reduce parallel per-client concurrency for long-generation jobs while we finish mitigation.

We are currently routing new traffic away from affected nodes and warming alternate pools with preserved KV caches. We'll also push a small config change to reduce the aggressiveness of the invalidation job.

I'll open a support bridge now and add Sam from SRE.

Mateo

[Quoted reply]

Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: [Redwood] Incident notification — mitigation & temporary workaround

Alex / team — Ben from Customer Success. We opened a bridge and Sam's team applied routing rules at 08:50 PT that reduced the 5xx window. As of 09:00 PT the error rate has dropped to near baseline and latency tails are improving.

What we recommend for you now:
- Apply client-side backoff (as Mateo suggested) for any in-flight workers.
- If you have a retry queue, delay retries by 2–5 minutes before reprocessing long-generation jobs to avoid creating a retry storm.
- If you'd like, we can pause non-critical scheduled generation jobs for 30–60 minutes while we complete the validation.

We'll follow up with a postmortem and timeline tomorrow including a set of recommended config changes for long-running customers.

— Ben
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: mitigation-checklist.txt]

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Brenner <alex@stellardata.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 10:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Post-incident follow-up: timeline & next steps (prefix cache invalidation)

Hi Alex / Taylor —

Thanks again for your patience yesterday. Engineering completed the internal incident review and we published the full timeline and remediation steps: https://drive.redwood.ai/records/PRJ-847/incident_timeline_v1.pdf and the status page has been updated to "Resolved".

Summary (short):
- Root cause: an automated prefix/KV cache invalidation job executed during a burst of long-sequence traffic, which caused increased CPU/memory pressure on a subset of hosting nodes and led to retries cascading into higher latency and a short 5xx window.
- Fixes implemented: reduced invalidation concurrency; improved warmup routing to avoid cold-KV penalties during cache churn; additional health checks to temporarily pause invalidation during sustained high load.
- Customer impact: Roughly 35 minutes of elevated latency for a subset of requests; peak 5xx rate affected ~0.8% of requests for <10 minutes.

Action items for us:
- We'll share a recommended client config that includes suggested backoff defaults and concurrency caps for long-generation jobs.
- We'll provide a small SDK patch to add jittered backoff helpers and an opt-in safety flag to reduce parallel long-sequence requests.

If you'd like a 30-minute technical walkthrough of the timeline and the mitigation plan, I'm happy to schedule one with our SRE lead and product engineer. Please let me know availability next week and we'll get it on the calendar.

Regards,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

[End of thread]
